sourceNotes: User-specified Compendium of Physical Activities MET constants; MET estimates gross energy and vary by pace, terrain, fitness, and technique.

heartRate.estimatedMaxFormula: 220 - ageYears (population estimate; individual error is substantial)

zones.cue: Conversational aerobic effort; useful for aerobic base and mitochondrial adaptation.
Controlled tempo; short phrases remain possible.
Hard to maximal VO2-oriented intervals; use sparingly with recovery.

heartRate.polarizedModel: Approximate 80% of endurance time easy/Zone 1-2 and 20% moderate-hard; distribution is a planning heuristic, not a rule for every beginner.
heartRate.breathing: A 3:2 footstep breathing rhythm can be tried at easy pace; switch to natural breathing if uncomfortable.

zeroTo3K: Week 1: 3 x 20-25 min walk/jog; jog 1 min, walk 2 min.
Week 2: 3 x 25 min; jog 2 min, walk 2 min.
Week 3: 3 x 25-30 min; jog 3 min, walk 90 sec.
Week 4: 3 easy sessions; build one continuous easy jog toward 3 km, repeat a week if needed.
3KTo5K: Weeks 1-2: 3 easy runs; extend one run by 0.5-1 km weekly.
Weeks 3-4: keep two easy runs and one short controlled tempo block (3 x 5 min).
Weeks 5-6: long easy run reaches 4-5 km; cut volume before an attempt.
5KTo10K: Weeks 1-2: 3 runs; easy volume increases at most about 5-10% if recovery is good.
Weeks 3-4: one easy long run, one conversational run, one light interval/tempo session.
Weeks 5-6: extend long run toward 7-8 km; preserve easy effort.
Weeks 7-8: reach 8-10 km comfortably, then taper before a timed effort.

continuousBlocks.progression: Begin with easy run-walk until continuous.
Add 3-5 minutes to one easy session weekly.
Keep two easy days; extend the long day gradually.
Only after 45 minutes is comfortable; avoid adding speed and duration together.

formCues.note: Use 165-175 steps/min only as an optional cue; natural cadence varies with height and pace. Do not force cadence.

roadmaps.pace: min/km = durationMinutes / distanceKm; use conversational effort on easy sessions rather than a fabricated pace target.

fatLossAndCardio: A moderate fat-loss pace is commonly around 0.5-0.8 kg/week for larger adults; adjust to body size, health, and recovery. Place demanding cardio away from heavy lifting when it harms strength; easy cardio after lifting or on separate days is acceptable. Track NEAT (steps and routine movement) consistently. Metabolic adaptation is managed with adherence review, sleep, and small adjustments—not crash dieting.
